static.solution: \frac{8 x + 4}{x^2-3x+2} = \frac{8 x+4}{(x-1)(x-2)} = \frac{A}{x-1} + \frac{B}{x-2}. Multiplying by (x-1) and (x-2), this becomes 8 x+4 = A(x-2)+B(x-1), or A+B = 8 \quad\hbox{and}\quad -2A - B = 4. Solving this system yields A = -12 and B = 20. Then \int\frac{8 x+4}{x^2-3x+2}dx = \int\left(\frac{20}{x-2} - \frac{12}{x-1}\right)\,dx = 20\ln\mathopen{}\left(\left|x-2\right|\right)-12\ln\mathopen{}\left(\left|x-1\right|\right)+C.
